Fresh three-thread ordering and cancellation validation
Fresh source-first isolated review after cancellation remediation

claims.text: The source asks for the coordination idea for the three modulo-3 thread sequences; finite limit, Java/Condition details and cancellation policy are not preserved source constraints.
Under the explicit finite-limit contract, fixed and 200 randomized-start stress executions emit exactly 1..limit and assign every value to its modulo-3 worker.
Shared cancellation plus wake-all prevents missing-owner deadlock when a waiting worker is interrupted or the output callback fails, and bounded joins verify clean termination.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=5 stress=200 randomized-start=true exact-order=true owner-partition=true interrupt-cancel=true output-failure-cancel=true timeout-clean=true
checks: 200 stress runs with randomized thread start order preserve exact global ordering
every value is emitted by the correct modulo-3 owner
interrupting a waiting worker cancels and wakes the collaboration group
an output callback failure cancels and wakes the collaboration group
all worker joins are bounded by timeout and leave no live thread

boundary_tests.expected: no output and all workers terminate
global sequence 1..limit and owner(value)=(value-1)%3 under shuffled starts

boundary_tests.case: worker 1 interrupted while awaiting its first turn
boundary_tests.expected: shared cancellation wakes all workers; no later thread waits for the departed owner
original runtime failure is propagated by its worker and the other workers terminate through shared cancellation

findings: The repository source recoverably asks only for the coordination design for three threads owning the 1,4,7... / 2,5,8... / 3,6,9... pattern; it does not preserve a finite limit, language, synchronization API, interruption contract, or callback-failure policy.
The candidate explicitly labels the finite limit and cancellation behavior as implementation/test contracts rather than source facts.
The lock-protected next state and modulo-3 owner predicate preserve one global sequence while assigning every value to the correct worker.
Fresh executable validation covers fixed limits and 200 deterministic randomized-start stress runs with bounded joins and exact sequence/ownership assertions.
The remediated shared cancelled state closes the missing-owner deadlock that otherwise occurs when a waiting worker is interrupted or the output callback throws.
The answer explains while-based Condition predicates, termination wakeups, failure semantics, alternatives, and tradeoffs without fabricating project experience.
No unsupported claim that Condition or the finite limit was mandated by the source remains.
